step1_figure.circuit_type: Rail-to-rail input operational amplifier with class AB output stage
step1_figure.description: An op-amp designed with parallel PMOS and NMOS differential input pairs to achieve an input common-mode range that extends beyond the power supply rails. It features a class AB push-pull output stage capable of driving heavy loads, and in the provided netlist, it is configured as a unity-gain voltage follower (as simulated in Figure 24.49).

open_loop_gain_base.description: Low-frequency open-loop gain of the base folded-cascode op-amp without gain enhancement.

equation.explanation: Product of the first stage (folded cascode) gain and the second stage (push-pull) gain.
equation.assumptions: Assumes output resistance is dominated by the parallel combination of the cascode devices and the output push-pull devices.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming typical SKY130 values at 10uA tail current: gm_n ≈ 0.5 mA/V, R_out1 ≈ 10 MΩ, gm_out ≈ 1 mA/V, R_out2 ≈ 10 kΩ. A_OLDC = (0.5m * 10M) * (1m * 10k) = 5000 * 10 = 50,000 V/V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Short-channel effects in SKY130 reduce intrinsic gain (lambda is high), so the gain will be lower than ideal long-channel textbook examples.

gain_enhancement_factor.description: Gain of the auxiliary amplifiers used for gain enhancement.

equation.explanation: The intrinsic gain of the auxiliary differential amplifiers used to regulate the cascode nodes.
equation.assumptions: Assumes symmetric N and P auxiliary amplifiers.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Simple diff-amps in SKY130 typically yield 20-30 dB of gain.

open_loop_gain_ge.description: Low-frequency open-loop gain with gain enhancement.

equation.explanation: The base open-loop gain multiplied by the gain of the enhancement amplifiers.
equation.assumptions: Assumes the GE amplifiers do not load the cascode nodes significantly.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Multiplicative effect of the auxiliary amplifier gain.

ge_amp_freq_response.description: Frequency response of the gain-enhancement amplifiers.

equation.explanation: Single-pole roll-off model for the auxiliary amplifiers.
equation.assumptions: Assumes a dominant pole in the GE amplifier.

sky130_expected.calculation: f_3dBGE depends on the parasitic capacitance at the GE amp output. Typically around 10-50 MHz in SKY130.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by the internal node parasitics of the GE stage.

open_loop_gain_ge_freq.description: Overall frequency response of the op-amp with gain enhancement.

equation.formula: A_OLGE(f) = (A_OLDC / (1 + j * f / f_3dB)) * (A_GEDC / (1 + j * f / f_3dBGE))
equation.explanation: Combined transfer function showing the doublet formed by the main op-amp pole and the GE amplifier pole.
equation.assumptions: Assumes no interaction between the poles.

sky130_expected.calculation: Creates a pole-zero doublet. The exact frequencies depend heavily on compensation.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Complex transfer function, highly dependent on specific C_c and C_cGE values.

dominant_pole_ge.description: Dominant pole frequency of the folded-cascode OTA with GE.

equation.explanation: The dominant pole is pushed to a lower frequency due to the increased output resistance from the GE amplifier.
equation.assumptions: Assumes C_c dominates the node capacitance.

sky130_expected.calculation: R_out ≈ 150 MΩ (with GE), C_c = 240 fF. f_3dB = 1 / (2 * pi * 150M * 240f) ≈ 4.4 kHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: High output resistance from GE significantly lowers the dominant pole.

ideal_regulated_voltage.description: Ideal output voltage of the op-amp when configured as a voltage regulator.

equation.explanation: The closed-loop gain of a non-inverting amplifier topology.

sky130_expected.calculation: For a follower (R_A = 0, R_B = infinity), V_REG = V_REF. If V_REF = 0.9V, V_REG = 0.9V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Directly follows the input reference in unity-gain configuration.

regulated_voltage_finite_gain.description: Actual regulated voltage accounting for finite open-loop gain.

equation.explanation: Shows the DC error introduced by the finite open-loop gain of the op-amp.

sky130_expected.reasoning: High open-loop gain keeps the DC error very small (sub-millivolt).

min_gate_voltage_regulator.description: Minimum voltage swing on the gate of the PMOS pass transistor in the regulator.

equation.explanation: Limits the drive strength of the output PMOS because its gate cannot swing all the way to ground in certain topologies.
equation.assumptions: Assumes all MOSFETs remain in saturation.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Threshold voltage of the NMOS limits the downward swing of the previous stage.

equation.assumptions: Assumes distinct first and second stages with dominant output resistances R1 and R2.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Matches the base open-loop gain calculation.

closed_loop_output_resistance.description: Output resistance of the op-amp in closed-loop configuration.

equation.explanation: The open-loop output resistance is divided by the loop gain.
equation.assumptions: Assumes loop gain (A_OLDC / A_CL) is much greater than 1.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Feedback drastically reduces the output impedance, making it a good voltage source.

closed_loop_pole_f2.description: Location of the output pole in closed-loop operation.

equation.formula: f_2 = A_OLDC / (2 * pi * R_2 * C_L * A_CL)
equation.explanation: The output pole is pushed to a higher frequency by the feedback loop.
equation.assumptions: Assumes R_out,CL dominates the time constant with C_L.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Feedback extends the bandwidth associated with the output node.

first_stage_pole_f1.description: Location of the pole at the output of the first stage.

equation.explanation: The dominant pole in an uncompensated or load-compensated two-stage amplifier.
equation.assumptions: Assumes C_gs of the second stage dominates the capacitance at node 1.

sky130_expected.reasoning: High impedance node combined with large gate capacitance of the output stage creates a low-frequency pole.

equation.formula: f_un = A_OLDC * f_2 = A_OLDC^2 / (2 * pi * R_2 * C_Lmin * A_CL)
equation.assumptions: Assumes single-pole roll-off up to f_un.

sky130_expected.calculation: Using standard gm/Cc approximation: gm ≈ 0.5 mA/V, Cc = 240 fF. f_un = 0.5m / (2 * pi * 240f) ≈ 331 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by the input transconductance and the compensation capacitor.

min_load_capacitance.description: Minimum load capacitance required for stability when load-compensated.

equation.formula: C_Lmin = ((g_m1 * R_1 * g_m2)^2 * R_2) / (2 * pi * f_un * A_CL)
equation.explanation: Calculates the minimum C_L needed to push the output pole low enough to act as the dominant compensation pole.
equation.assumptions: Assumes the op-amp is compensated by the load capacitance rather than a Miller capacitor.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Load compensation requires a massive capacitor to ensure stability, often too large for on-chip integration.

slew_rate.description: Maximum rate of change of the output voltage.

equation.explanation: Slew rate is limited by the tail current charging the compensation capacitor.
equation.assumptions: Assumes the input stage fully switches the tail current into the compensation branch.

sky130_expected.calculation: I_tail ≈ 20 uA, C_c = 240 fF. SR = 20u / 240f = 83.3 V/us.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Matches the fast step response seen in Figure 24.49 (800mV in ~10ns).

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure open-loop gain, phase margin, unity-gain frequency, slew rate, and input common-mode range of the rail-to-rail op-amp configured as a voltage follower.
